object_description: three articulated buildings stepped over three levels at the top of the site
design_condition: the ensemble sits at the top of the site and takes advantage of the topography, interacting with the existing buildings to reinforce the hamlet character, with horizontal paths linking the functions across the whole site

positive: The project asserts the existing built and landscape components while respecting the uses and spatial sequences of the site
Three articulated buildings interact with the existing fabric and reinforce the character of the hamlet
The site is designed as a whole, with horizontal paths linking the various functions
Parking and the future school are integrated as components contributing to the intrinsic quality of the site
The three levels take advantage of the topography to offer age-appropriate connections to the outdoors
The lower ground floor gives the youngest easy access to the garden
The double-height refectory provides a visual link with the floor above
The functions are organised to ensure optimal operation
The sober architectural expression of facade and roof blends naturally into the existing fabric while evoking the programme
Volume and compactness place the project in a highly favourable position economically and in sustainability terms
The proposed layout of the future school complements the existing fabric well
Very precise integration and high quality urban design enhance the site as a whole
negative: The location of the reading and rest area deserves to be in a quieter zone given its function
The layout of the future school remains subject to road boundary constraints
